title: Group Text: WWTP Yard Drains Backing Up, PS2 Falling Behind

bubbles.text: WWTP Shift Op: Photo attached: yard drain grate by Clarifier 2, water bubbling up around it, wet pavement running toward the SCADA building.

WWTP Shift Op: Water coming up through the yard drains by the clarifiers, about 2 inches and spreading toward the SCADA building. There's a wet line along the bottom of the SCADA room door. River's 22.1. It's the interior ponding, not the river.

WWTP Shift Op: Two of the six chemical totes (the bisulfite ones) are still on the low pad and the mobile generator is still on its trailer by the shop. Flatbed is back from Hollow Court but the driver's off shift at 10:00. Plant is still treating, all processes normal for now.
PS2 Operator: District, PS2. Both 24-inch units are running flat out and the sump is still gaining. Hollow Creek interior ditch is up 0.4 ft since 06:00.

PS2 Operator: We can't keep up with the seepage plus the rain ponding. If I don't get one of the portable pumps down here, the low ground by the plant keeps filling. Same message going out on channel 4.

instructorNote: Core inject: water inside the levee has reached the plant's SCADA floor level, which matches 22.5 ft at the gauge, while the river reads only 22.1 ft. The WWTP should move the totes, generator, portable pumps and spares above the plant's flood line before the flatbed driver goes off shift at 10:00, keep treating, and set the shutdown-and-bypass trigger off the latest forecast, with EM and PIO told first and the Iowa DNR notice sent through the EOC. Watch whether LEV decides to send one of the two portable pumps from PS1 to PS2 and tells the EOC the pumps are falling behind the ponding.
